workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer alleges the cardholder cancelled their FluxFit Online subscription on 18 March 2025 but was still charged £29.99 on 20 April 2025. To defend under Visa 13.2, the merchant must prove all four: (1) terms disclosing the recurring billing and how to cancel, (2) advance notice of the upcoming charge where the amount exceeds the threshold, (3) no record of a cancellation request before the billing date, and (4) the cardholder's original opt-in to recurring billing.

pointers.quote:
Subscriptions auto-renew
monthly at the rate disclosed at signup until cancelled. Members may cancel at any time via their
account dashboard or by emailing support@fluxfit.example.

requirements.reasoning: The published terms disclose monthly auto-renewal and two cancellation methods (dashboard or email). This proves only what the terms say. It does not prove the cardholder saw or accepted them, which falls under requirement 4.

The terms state a policy of emailing members at least 5 days before renewal, but no notification email, send log or delivery record for this cardholder's 20 April renewal was supplied. A policy is not proof the notice was sent. The stated 5-day window is also shorter than the typical 7-day expectation.
No account activity log, dashboard cancellation history or support-inbox search was provided. Nothing addresses the cardholder's claim of a cancellation on 18 March 2025.

No signup record, checkbox or consent log, timestamp, or initial transaction record shows this cardholder opted in to recurring billing. The terms' statement 'By subscribing to FluxFit Online, members agree' is generic policy, not evidence of this cardholder's consent.

workup.action_justification: Only the terms requirement is met; the other three rest on account and email records the merchant should hold and can supply.
evidence_to_request: Account activity/audit log for the cardholder covering at least 1 March 2025 to 20 April 2025, showing no cancellation via the dashboard, with timestamps
Search results of the support@fluxfit.example inbox and ticketing system for any contact or cancellation request from the cardholder's email address before 20 April 2025
Email send/delivery log and a copy of the renewal notification sent to the cardholder before the 20 April 2025 charge, showing send date and recipient address
Original signup record: date and time, the recurring-billing consent checkbox or acknowledgement, the terms version presented, and the initial transaction reference
Confirmation of the cardholder's billing cycle anchor date and full billing history for the subscription
workup.rationale: The merchant has supplied only its published Membership Terms (terms_v3.2), which disclose monthly auto-renewal and the dashboard and email cancellation methods. There is no evidence that a renewal notice was sent to this cardholder before the 20 April 2025 charge. There is no record addressing the cardholder's stated cancellation on 18 March 2025, and no record of the cardholder's original opt-in to recurring billing. Visa 13.2 requires all four requirements, so the case cannot be represented on the current file. The merchant has been asked for account logs, support-inbox records, notification send logs and the signup consent record.
caveats: The cardholder claims cancellation on 18 March 2025. Under the merchant's own terms, cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing period, so if the billing anchor is the 20th, a 18 March cancellation would have stopped the 20 April renewal. The merchant's evidence must show no cancellation occurred, not merely that one was deferred.
The terms promise 5 days' renewal notice, below the typical 7-day expectation. Confirm whether £29.99 falls above or below the applicable notification threshold.
The terms document is version 3.2, published February 2025. Confirm which terms version was in force and presented at the cardholder's original signup, which may predate February 2025.
AVS Y, CVV M and frictionless 3DS confirm the cardholder's card and authentication on the transaction. These are not relevant to a cancellation dispute and do not substitute for any 13.2 requirement.
The terms clause that failure to receive a notification is not grounds for refund does not override the scheme's notification requirement.

rule_text:
Visa 13.2 - Cancelled Recurring Transaction
Issuer claim: Cardholder cancelled a recurring subscription but was still charged.
Logic: ALL 4 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. Terms of service disclosing the recurring billing arrangement and the cancellation method
  2. Evidence the cardholder was notified of the upcoming charge (typically 7+ days in advance) for transactions over a defined threshold
  3. No record of the cardholder having submitted a cancellation request prior to the billing date
  4. Evidence of the cardholder's original opt-in to the recurring arrangement
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: frictionless
Shipping vs billing postcode: no shipping postcode on file (digital goods or service)
Chargeback raised 15 days after the transaction
